integrity.interpretation: The session-local ring buffer reports no discarded or overwritten chunks. The global traced_chunks_discarded stat remains nonzero and its producer/owner is unresolved; no attribution is claimed for that global count.

firstOpen.limits: Only 2 of the 4 first-open missed frames have a matching RenderThread slice.

frameTimeline.interpretation: In this dark isolated motion-host capture, App Deadline Missed rows coincide with high scheduled main/UI-thread work (about 16.8-31.5ms median across the three groups). This supports UI-thread work as a contributor to deadline misses in this fixture, but the trace does not identify a Kotlin method or establish the same cause in release/R8 or real MainActivity. Dropped Frame rows have low matched UI and RenderThread running time and remain unattributed.

renderThreadBufferWait.interpretation: DrawFrames-descendant waitForBufferRelease slices occur on many close frames but none of the 10 close App Deadline Missed frames; they reflect buffer pacing/backpressure in this trace and are not evidence that GPU wait caused the observed deadline misses.

conclusion: This is a useful partial attribution: session-local trace buffer integrity is clean; the repeated global discarded counter remains unexplained; App Deadline Missed frames correlate with main/UI-thread CPU occupancy in this motion fixture; GPU completion/buffer backpressure appears but did not overlap the marked close deadline misses; dropped-frame and release-build causes remain open. It does not establish stable performance improvement.
next: Continue remaining page/panel and continuous-transition comparisons. For performance work, isolate main-thread work on an R8 MainActivity path and separately explain the producer/service-level discarded counter before any optimization-benefit claim.
